title: Pipeline Clarity: Per-route/Model/Customer Cost & Latency Breakdown Service
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a production-grade service that computes and serves explainable cost and latency breakdowns scoped by route_id, model_variant, and customer_id. Inputs: streaming telemetry (tokens, spans, model variant used, start/end timestamps), pricing ledger, and routing metadata. Outputs: time-windowed breakdowns consumed by Console dashboards, billing reconciler, and alerting. Must support near-real-time queries (95th percentile under 1s for cached routes), deterministic batch backfills, and stable schemas for downstream reconciliations. Key goals: clear provenance for every cost row, compatibility with Dedicated/Private model variants, and graceful degradation to coarse-grained summaries when data is partial.
acceptance_criteria: API returns per-route/per-model/per-customer breakdown for a 1h window within 1s for cached responses and within 6s for cold queries
Breakdown rows contain provenance: source_telemetry_id, price_version, aggregation_window, and sample_count
Backfill job can recompute any 30d range within SLA (48h) and produce identical canonical ids used by realtime service
Unit tests cover price-version changes, token deduplication edge cases, and late-arriving telemetry (>24h)
End-to-end integration: Grafana dashboard shows parity between new service and legacy rollup within 1% for a randomized 7-day sample
technical_notes: Streaming-first architecture: Flink for per-route incremental aggregates + Beam-compatible batch jobs for deterministic backfills
Shard by (customer_id % 128, route_id) to bound per-partition state growth; use TTL for inactive route partitions
Deduplicate tokens using telemetry_event_id + model_request_id; assign deterministic canonical_id for join stability
Pricing join uses immutable price_version keys; changes create new rows instead of mutating historical records
Materialize hourly rollups to TimescaleDB for low-latency Console reads and keep raw streaming sink in parquet for audits/backfills
Metric tags: cost_cents, user_perceived_latency_ms, model_compute_latency_ms, queuing_latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out
Fallback: when KV cache data missing, mark 'cache_coverage: partial' and expose both estimated and observed cost columns
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Spike completed comparing Flink vs Spark Structured Streaming for incremental join latency. Team chose Flink for lower per-record latency and state TTL semantics.
2025-02-22: Schema v1 agreed in design review—includes price_version, telemetry_event_id, canonical_id, window_start. Action: prod-read schema doc on Confluence.
2025-02-25: Implemented prototype Flink job that consumes telemetry topic and emits hourly rollups to staging TimescaleDB. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4892
2025-02-27: Design review feedback from PM (Aisha Kapoor): add explicit column for 'estimated_cost' vs 'observed_cost' to simplify reconciliation. Accepted; updated schema.
2025-02-28: Load test with synthetic 10k RPS telemetry showed 12% tail latency under current shard config; plan to increase partitioning to 256. Follow-up: ENG-81305 to tune state backend.
2025-03-01: QA plan drafted and test harness for late-arriving messages added. Next: set up nightly backfill run and integration with billing reconciler sandbox.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy to staging cluster, validate parity dashboard between legacy rollups and new service for 7 days
Stage 2: Canary in prod for 5% of customer traffic (low-risk routes) with read-only flag for Console
Stage 3: Enable read-path for Console for all routes and run parallel backfills for 90d historical windows
Stage 4: Flip default charts to new service after 14-day parity window and ops signoff
qa_plan: Integration tests that replay recorded telemetry and assert canonical_id stability
Load tests using k6 to simulate 20k RPS and verify partitioning behavior
Reconciliation job comparing output against billing sandbox; alert if >2% drift on sample set
Chaos test: simulate late messages and broker reorder to validate watermark handling
notes_on_scaling: Estimate peak state size: 200GB per 128 shards for active routes; use RocksDB with incremental checkpointing
Plan autoscaling for Flink taskmanagers based on per-shard incoming msg rate and TTL eviction rates
Materialized view compaction: daily compaction job to collapse hourly rollups to daily retention table to reduce read load
follow_up_tasks: ENG-81305: Tune Flink state backend and increase partitioning to 256
ENG-81522: Add price-version migration job and schema migrator for historical adjustments
ENG-81670: Build Console read cache layer to serve sub-second reads for frequent dashboards
ENG-81701: Create runbook for partial-data fallbacks and SRE alerting thresholds
final_notes: Focus on deterministic outputs for reconciliations. Keep schema forward-compatible and document provenance for every cost row. Prioritize small, observable releases to limit blast radius.
